articles.title: Decision Models vs Chat Models: Route a Task Without Writing an Essay
articles.excerpt: Many model calls do not need a paragraph. A support ticket arrives, and the application needs a queue name, a yes-or-no flag, or a score from a small ordered scale. Asking a chat model for an explanat…
articles.body: Many model calls do not need a paragraph. A support ticket arrives, and the application needs a queue name, a yes-or-no flag, or a score from a small ordered scale. Asking a chat model for an explanation and then parsing its prose adds work and creates another place for formatting to go wrong. Ollama introduced a Jev-style decision endpoint in version 0.35, announced on September 29, 2026. The /v1/systemone API accepts a state object and named questions, such as a choice among fixed labels or a yes/no question. Treat it as a typed classification interface: useful when the set of answers is known in advance, but still a model prediction that needs application checks. See Ollama’s decision model announcement and the System One API reference .

articles.title: 1,000/1,000 bits leaked through a rounding error
articles.excerpt: 1,000/1,000 bits leaked through a rounding error Two sandboxed models with no shared filesystem and no messaging exchanged 1,221 out of 1,221 messages anyway. I rebuilt the trick in NumPy and decoded…
articles.body: 1,000/1,000 bits leaked through a rounding error Two sandboxed models with no shared filesystem and no messaging exchanged 1,221 out of 1,221 messages anyway. I rebuilt the trick in NumPy and decoded 1,000 out of 1,000 bits — through a rounding error of 0.00003. The paper that sent me here Niranjan Deshpande and David Africa posted "Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed" to LessWrong on November 19. It hit Hacker News' front page today at 311 points, and it deserves the attention: two agents running on the same vLLM inference server can reliably communicate even if they cannot send each other messages or access the same filesystem. The channels are side channels — mechanisms that let one model subtly affect another model's computation.

articles.excerpt: Most astrology MVPs start the same way: pick an ephemeris library or a WASM wrapper, get a chart on screen in a weekend, and look at the license only when the app is about to ship. That is the week th…
articles.body: Most astrology MVPs start the same way: pick an ephemeris library or a WASM wrapper, get a chart on screen in a weekend, and look at the license only when the app is about to ship. That is the week the question becomes urgent. This post is a checklist, not legal advice. Read the actual license text of whatever you use, and ask a lawyer if money depends on it. 1. Know which of three license families you are in Permissive (MIT, BSD, Apache 2.0). You can ship closed-source commercial code. Keep the notice files. Copyleft (GPL, AGPL). GPL obligations start when you distribute. AGPL adds a network clause: if users interact over a network with a modified version, which usually includes a program built on the library, you may have to offer them its full source.

articles.body: 2.25: the matrix exponent is final. I measured 2.99 OpenAI proved the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4 — ω = 2.25, not 2. On my machine, the same multiplication still scales like n^2.99. Both numbers are true, and the gap between them is the whole story. The result On November 24, OpenAI posted "The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths" — a paper proving that ω = 9/4 over every field. The upper bound, ω ≤ 9/4, was already known: OpenAI's own preprint from October 2 established it over ℂ, and Amanov, van den Berg and Zuiddam extended it to every field.

articles.title: Which AI Is Really Behind That Chatbot? I Fingerprinted 3 Live Bots With LLMmap, and It Was Confidently Wrong
articles.excerpt: Every company is shipping a chatbot. Banks, telecoms, airlines, your landlord's property app. Almost none of them tell you which AI model is running underneath. For an attacker, that question matters…
articles.body: Every company is shipping a chatbot. Banks, telecoms, airlines, your landlord's property app. Almost none of them tell you which AI model is running underneath. For an attacker, that question matters a lot. Every model family has its own weaknesses: jailbreaks that work on one model fail on another, and safety tuning varies from vendor to vendor. Knowing the model is the reconnaissance step before the attack, the same way knowing a server runs an old Apache version tells you which exploits to try. So I ran an experiment. I took LLMmap , an open-source tool from a peer-reviewed security paper, and pointed it at three live chatbots . The short version: One bot revealed its model family when I asked a few simple questions.

articles.body: After a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25). The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024 . Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos , a " rubble pile" asteroid , and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test , which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid. Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
articles.excerpt: The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.
articles.body: The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun.

articles.body: The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze. November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons , which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.
